sources.title: Ministry of Education parent learning portal
Māori history in The 2007 New Zealand Curriculum

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: NZ coins and change
topics.description: Use NZ dollars and cents to represent small amounts and reason about change.
evidence: Represent the price with coins
Explain a small subtraction as change
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} represent the price with coins and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A pretend dairy shop with NZD price cards.
nz.parentActivity: Make paper price cards and use clean coins or drawings to buy one item at a time.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Metric measures at home
topics.description: Choose centimetres for length and millilitres for liquid quantities in familiar objects.
evidence: Select a suitable unit
Read a marked scale with support
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} select a suitable unit and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: Metric units used in NZ homes.
nz.parentActivity: Measure a lunchbox with a ruler and compare marked volumes of water in a measuring jug.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Sharing kai fairly
topics.description: Connect equal sharing with halves and quarters using visual models.
evidence: Make equal halves and quarters
Explain why unequal pieces are not equal shares
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make equal halves and quarters and explain their reasoning?

nz.parentActivity: Cut paper food shapes into equal parts and explain how each person receives the same share.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Reading a bus timetable
topics.description: Read a sample bus timetable and calculate waiting and journey times.
evidence: Read departure and arrival times
Calculate a duration across an hour boundary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} read departure and arrival times and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A fictional NZ public transport timetable; not live travel advice.
nz.parentActivity: Create three departure times and ask which bus arrives before a chosen activity starts.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Comparing supermarket unit prices
topics.description: Compare package prices by converting them to a common quantity.
evidence: Convert two prices to the same quantity
Explain the comparison with units
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} convert two prices to the same quantity and explain their reasoning?

nz.parentActivity: Compare two invented cereal prices per 100 g and explain when a larger pack is better value.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Planning a whānau outing budget
topics.description: Plan an outing within a fixed budget and explain trade-offs.
evidence: Calculate the total cost
Justify one choice within the budget
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} calculate the total cost and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A fictional local outing with transport, food and entry costs.
nz.parentActivity: Give a pretend NZ$60 budget and several clearly invented options; calculate the total and money left.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Rainfall and temperature graphs
topics.description: Represent a small weather dataset and explain what the graph shows.
evidence: Label axes with units
Support a comparison using the data
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} label axes with units and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A fictional week of NZ weather, explicitly labelled sample data.
nz.parentActivity: Record or invent seven days of rainfall, draw a bar graph and compare the wettest days.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: School travel survey
topics.description: Group anonymous travel responses and discuss the limits of a small sample.
evidence: Produce accurate category counts
Explain why a small sample cannot represent every NZ child
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} produce accurate category counts and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: Walking, cycling, bus and car travel to a fictional school.
nz.parentActivity: Use ten fictional responses without names or addresses, then tally and graph the categories.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Map scale and a local walking route
topics.description: Use a map scale to estimate a route distance and distinguish map distance from travel time.
evidence: Use the scale consistently
State why the result is an estimate
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} use the scale consistently and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A public map of a local park, with no home location shared.
nz.parentActivity: Measure a simple route on a printed map with a scale bar and convert it to metres or kilometres.

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: NZ native and endemic species
topics.description: Distinguish native, endemic and introduced species using sourced NZ examples.
evidence: Distinguish native from endemic
Support a species claim with a source
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} distinguish native from endemic and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: DOC information about local plants and animals.
nz.parentActivity: Choose three species from DOC pages and record their habitat and origin status with the source.

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: A local bush food web
topics.description: Connect plants, insects and birds in a simple food web, checking specific feeding claims.
evidence: Identify a producer and consumers
Explain one possible effect of a change in the web
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} identify a producer and consumers and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A NZ bush ecosystem studied through public species information.
nz.parentActivity: Draw a small food web from verified feeding examples and explain the meaning of each arrow.

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Water through a local catchment
topics.description: Trace rainfall, runoff and evaporation through a simple catchment model.
evidence: Connect runoff and the water cycle
Explain where water may collect or move
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} connect runoff and the water cycle and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A drawn NZ hillside, stream and coast.
nz.parentActivity: Draw the path of rain from a hill to a stream and sea; add evaporation without visiting waterways.

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Matariki, Puanga and observing seasons
topics.description: Explore seasonal observation and regional Matariki and Puanga traditions using attributed sources.
evidence: Recognise that regional traditions vary
Attribute a cultural explanation to its source
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} recognise that regional traditions vary and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: Different iwi may observe different stars and traditions.
nz.parentActivity: Read Te Papa’s regional guide together and separate an astronomical observation from a named cultural account.

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Histories of local place names
topics.description: Investigate one local place name using reliable and attributed historical accounts.
evidence: Identify the source of an account
Distinguish a sourced meaning from a guess
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} identify the source of an account and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A place chosen by the family; meanings must be sourced, not guessed.
nz.parentActivity: Find a council, museum or mana whenua account of a place name and record what it says and what remains uncertain.

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Comparing historical accounts in Aotearoa
topics.description: Compare how two attributed accounts describe an event and separate evidence from interpretation.
evidence: Identify agreement and differences
Explain how the source affects an interpretation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} identify agreement and differences and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: Age-appropriate Aotearoa histories selected with a parent or teacher.
nz.parentActivity: Choose two short public accounts, note their authors and dates, then compare shared facts and perspectives.

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Community decisions and public services
topics.description: Consider how a community can weigh needs and make a shared decision.
evidence: Describe more than one perspective
Give a reasoned proposal and acknowledge a trade-off
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe more than one perspective and explain their reasoning?

nz.localContext: A fictional NZ library or park improvement discussion.
nz.parentActivity: Choose between three imaginary park improvements within a budget and explain whose needs each serves.
